docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
I’m a Technical Writer based in Buenos Aires, with over five years of experience creating clear, user-focused documentation for software products. I work closely with subject matter experts, developers, product teams, and other stakeholders to understand complex concepts and turn them into documentation that is useful and accessible to its intended audience.

I hold a Bachelor’s degree in Translation from the University of Buenos Aires, where I specialized in legal translation. Although legal translation and technical writing may seem like very different fields, that background taught me something that has become central to my work as a Technical Writer: how to make complex information easier to understand and approach.

Before becoming a Technical Writer, I led AI data training projects, working with clients from different countries and coordinating with internal teams and project participants throughout the project lifecycle. This gave me valuable experience working across teams and communicating with people in different roles and professional backgrounds.

I’ve also completed a course in Natural Language Processing (NLP), and I’m currently pursuing a Master’s degree in Translation and New Technologies.

I’m interested in the intersection of language, technology, and in how new technologies are changing the way we create, manage, and communicate technical information.

docs.title: Technical writing
docs.text:
Technical writing is about making knowledge accessible and useful to the people who need it. That might mean helping users understand a product, helping technical teams understand a process, or capturing valuable knowledge for the company that would otherwise remain in people’s heads. It can also provide transparency into how products, processes, and systems work.

For me, this means treating documentation as a product. It should evolve alongside the product it describes, staying useful, accurate, and representative of what the product actually is. When documentation is disconnected from the product, it can quickly become outdated and difficult to trust.

I also believe documentation should have a clear purpose. Not every piece of information needs to become documentation, and not every organization has the same documentation needs. The decision to invest in documentation should come from an actual need within the product or organization. When that need exists, the Technical Writer’s role is to turn that need into documentation that provides real value.

Ultimately, good documentation part of how a product communicates with the people who use and build it.

docs.title: How to Install Loom on Google Chrome
docs.text:
Loom is a tool designed to create videos. With a few simple steps, you can record a tutorial, record yourself, or capture any type of video you want.

You can use Loom as a desktop application or install it as a Google Chrome extension. This guide covers the steps to add the extension to Chrome.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • Google Chrome installed on your computer

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open Google Chrome and go to the Chrome Web Store.
  2. In the search bar, type Loom and press Enter.
  3. Look for the official Loom extension — it has a purple logo and the description "Screen & Video Recording." Make sure it's published by "Loom" to avoid fake extensions.
  4. Click the extension, then click Add to Chrome.
  5. A confirmation popup will appear. Click Add extension to confirm.
  6. Chrome may prompt you to allow camera, microphone, and screen-sharing permissions. Click Allow for each one to enable full recording functionality.

Tip

If you don't see the Loom icon in your toolbar after installing, click the puzzle-piece icon next to the address bar, find Loom, and click the pin icon to keep it visible for easy access.

  1. Click the Loom icon in your toolbar and sign in with your existing account, or sign up for free if you're new to Loom.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Once signed in, click the Loom icon again — you should see options to record your screen, camera, or both. If this menu appears, the installation was successful.

docs.title: Open-Meteo API: Endpoint Reference
docs.text: Quick reference for two Open-Meteo endpoints: current weather and location search.

docs.title: Current Weather
docs.text:
Returns current weather conditions for a given coordinate pair.

Base URL: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description latitude float Yes Latitude of the location longitude float Yes Longitude of the location current string Yes Comma-separated list of variables to return (e.g. temperature_2m,wind_speed_10m)

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text: GET https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=-34.6&longitude=-58.4&current=temperature_2m,wind_speed_10m

docs.title: Example Response
docs.text:
{
  "latitude": -34.622143,
  "longitude": -58.40909,
  "timezone": "GMT",
  "elevation": 23.0,
  "current_units": {
    "temperature_2m": "°C",
    "wind_speed_10m": "km/h"
  },
  "current": {
    "time": "2026-09-22T22:45",
    "temperature_2m": 10.2,
    "wind_speed_10m": 6.4
  }
}

Note

  • elevation is returned in meters and reflects the terrain elevation at the given coordinates, not the request altitude.
  • Values inside current depend entirely on what was listed in the current parameter — omitted variables won't appear in the response.

docs.title: Location Search (Geocoding)
docs.text:
Searches for locations by name and returns matching coordinates, useful for resolving a city name before calling the weather endpoint above.

Base URL: https://geocoding-api.open-meteo.com/v1/search

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description name string Yes — Location name or postal code. Minimum 2 characters. count integer No 10 Number of results to return (max 100) format string No json Response format (json or protobuf)

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text: GET https://geocoding-api.open-meteo.com/v1/search?name=Berlin

docs.title: Example Response
docs.text:
{
  "results": [
    {
      "id": 2950159,
      "name": "Berlin",
      "latitude": 52.52437,
      "longitude": 13.41053,
      "country": "Germany",
      "timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
      "population": 3426354
    },
    {
      "id": 5083330,
      "name": "Berlin",
      "latitude": 44.46867,
      "longitude": -71.18508,
      "country": "United States",
      "timezone": "America/New_York",
      "population": 9367
    }
  ]
}

Note

  • The search is name-based, not location-based. Searching "Berlin" returns every place named Berlin worldwide, not just the German capital. Sort or filter results by population or country if you need the most prominent match.
  • A two-character search matches exact names only; three or more characters use prefix matching.
  • Narrow results by appending a country or region to the name parameter, e.g. name=Berlin, Germany.
